title: Drug Rediscovery for Rare Immune Mediated Inflammatory Diseases
off: Drug Rediscovery for Rare Immune Mediated Inflammatory Diseases

officials.n: Jaap M van Laar, Prof. dr.

summary: Research into novel therapies for rare, immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs) is limited due to small patient populations. Patients with Behçet's disease (BD), idiopathic inflammatory myopathy (IIM, also known as myositis) and IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) are treated with high-dosed glucocorticoids, methotrexate, azathioprine and mycophenolate mofetil, mostly for long periods of time with attendant risks of long-term toxicity, including infections. Therefore, there is an urgent need for new, more specific anti-inflammatory therapies such as targeted synthetic and biological disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs. Due to the role of type 1 interferon in both BD, IIM and IgG4-RD, JAK-STAT inhibition may be a promising treatment strategy in these conditions, because JAK1 is critical for the signal transduction of pro-inflammatory cytokine receptors. Previous research showed that JAK1 inhibition reduces activation of type 1 interferon-regulated proteins and key chemokines that control tissue inflammation.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 years of older
* One of the following rare IMIDs:

  * Diagnosis of Behçet's disease without refractory life, organ or sight-threatening symptoms with active disease, defined as a BDCAF \>2 (new BDCAF) or \>15 (old BDCAF) or with active disease, based on clinical grounds (e.g. the need to start new or additional medication
  * Diagnosis of idiopathic inflammatory myopathy, according to diagnostic criteria:

Dermatomyositis: Dermatomyositis Classification Criteria according to the European Neuromuscular Centre guidelines 201852 or anti-synthetase syndrome: Anti- synthetase syndrome Classification Criteria according to the European Neuromuscular Centre guidelines 200353, both with active disease, defined as a CDASI score of ≥5 or abnormal levels of at least 1 of the following enzymes: creatine kinase (≥ 4× upper limit of normal \[ULN\]), aldolase (≥4 × ULN), lactate dehydrogenase (LDH ≥4 × ULN), aspartate transaminase (AST ≥4 × ULN), alanine aminotransferase (ALT ≥4 × ULN) or a MRI within the last 3 months indicative of active inflammation (e.g. edema signal pattern in affected proximal muscles) or active disease based on clinical grounds, e.g. the need to start new or additional medication

* Diagnosis of IgG4-related disease, according to 2019 ACR/EULAR guidelines, with active disease, defined as: IgG4-related disease responder index \>10 or active disease based on clinical grounds, e.g. the need to start new or additional medication

  * Refractory disease, defined as symptomatic disease that persists despite a 12-week trial of glucocorticoid therapy as well as lack of response to at least one other immunosuppressive agent such as methotrexate (MTX), mycophenolate mofetil (MMF), azathioprine (AZA) or rituximab or intolerance to standard-of-care treatment, as defined by the treating physician.
  * No evidence of active or latent or inadequately treated infection with mycobacterium tuberculosis (TB) as defined by all of the following: both a negative QuantiFERON-TB Gold (QFT-G) In-Tube test and a Mantoux tuberculin skin test performed at or within 3 months prior to screening and no signs suggestive of active TB infection as determined (and documented) by a qualified radiologist or pulmonologist as per local standard of care on a chest radiograph and no history of either untreated or inadequately treated latent or active TB infection.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Age \<18 years
* Age ≥65 years
* Life expectancy less than 6 months
* Juvenile DM, myositis overlapping with other autoimmune diseases, immune mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM), inclusion-body myositis or cancer-associated myositis
* End-stage IIM wherein muscle weakness is most likely due to muscle damage, rather than myositis disease activity
* Increased risk of major cardiovascular problems
* Current smoker or smoked for a long time in the past
* Pregnancy or lactation
* Previous use of other JAK inhibitors
* Use of any investigational drug within one month prior to screening or within five half-lives of the investigational agent, whichever is longer.
* Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) infection
* Presence of an active infection or viral hepatitis type B or C
* History of shingles or recurrent herpes simplex infection
* Concomitant malignancies or previous malignancies within the last five years (with exception of adequately treated basal or squamous cell carcinoma of the skin)
* Increased risk of cancer
* Kidney injury with estimated glomerular filtration rate \<15mL/min/1.73m2
* Liver failure Child Pugh C
* Absolute neutrophil count \<1\*109
* Absolute leukocyte count \<0.5\*109
* Hemoglobin \<5mmol/L - Inability to comply with study and/or follow-up procedures
* Known recent substance abuse (drugs or alcohol).
* Poor tolerability of venipuncture or lack of adequate venous access for required blood sampling during the study period.
* Previous non-adherence to immunosuppressants
* Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients
* Rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption

arms.d: 26 weeks of Filgotinib once daily, 200mg, orally,

x.titre: Filgotinib dans la maladie de Behçet, les myosites et la maladie à IgG4
x.question: L'inhibition de JAK1 par le filgotinib réduit-elle l'activité de maladies inflammatoires rares (Behçet, myopathies inflammatoires, maladie à IgG4) ?
x.contexte:
La maladie de Behçet, les myopathies inflammatoires idiopathiques (dermatomyosite, syndrome des anti-synthétases) et la maladie à IgG4 sont des maladies inflammatoires à médiation immune rares. Leur traitement repose sur de fortes doses de corticoïdes, le méthotrexate, l'azathioprine et le mycophénolate, souvent de façon prolongée avec une toxicité cumulée, notamment infectieuse.

La rareté de ces maladies freine le développement de nouveaux médicaments. Une stratégie de « redécouverte » consiste à tester dans plusieurs maladies rares un traitement déjà développé ailleurs, ici dans la polyarthrite rhumatoïde et les maladies inflammatoires de l'intestin.

Le filgotinib est un inhibiteur préférentiel de JAK1. La voie JAK-STAT transmet le signal de nombreuses cytokines pro-inflammatoires, dont les interférons de type 1, impliqués dans ces trois maladies. Des travaux antérieurs ont montré que l'inhibition de JAK1 réduit l'activation de protéines régulées par l'interféron et de chimiokines clés de l'inflammation tissulaire.

Cet essai de phase 2 ouvert, à bras unique, promu par l'UMC Utrecht, traite pendant 26 semaines par filgotinib 200 mg/j des patients de 18 à 65 ans ayant une maladie active, réfractaire (myosite, IgG4) ou non menaçante (Behçet). Les critères d'activité sont spécifiques de chaque maladie.
x.interet: L'étude pourrait donner un premier signal d'efficacité d'un inhibiteur de JAK1 dans ces trois maladies orphelines, avant tout essai comparatif. La taille réduite (60 patients) et l'absence de groupe contrôle limitent la portée des résultats.
x.profil: Des adultes de 18 à 65 ans ayant une maladie de Behçet, une dermatomyosite/un syndrome des anti-synthétases ou une maladie à IgG4 active.
inclusion: Behçet actif sans atteinte menaçante (BDCAF > 2 ou > 15 selon la version) ou nécessité d'un nouveau traitement
Dermatomyosite ou syndrome des anti-synthétases (critères ENMC) actifs (CDASI ≥ 5, enzymes musculaires ≥ 4 N, IRM active ou besoin clinique de traitement)
Maladie à IgG4 (critères ACR/EULAR 2019) active (IgG4-RD RI > 10 ou besoin de traitement)
Maladie réfractaire : persistance après 12 semaines de corticoïdes et échec d'au moins un autre immunosuppresseur, ou intolérance
Absence de tuberculose active, latente ou mal traitée (QuantiFERON et IDR négatifs, radiographie thoracique)
exclusion: Âge ≥ 65 ans, espérance de vie < 6 mois
Dermatomyosite juvénile, myosite en chevauchement, MNMI, myosite à inclusions ou paranéoplasique, myosite en stade terminal
Risque cardiovasculaire majeur, tabagisme actif ou ancien important, risque accru de cancer ou cancer < 5 ans
Traitement antérieur par un autre inhibiteur de JAK ou médicament expérimental récent
VIH, hépatite B ou C, infection active, antécédent de zona ou d'herpès récurrent
Grossesse ou allaitement, DFG < 15 mL/min, insuffisance hépatique Child-Pugh C, cytopénies
Mauvaise observance antérieure, abus de substances, hypersensibilité au filgotinib

bras.traitement: 200 mg par voie orale une fois par jour pendant 26 semaines

x.critere: Qualité de vie (EQ-5D-5L) et activité de chaque maladie (Behçet, myosite, IgG4) à 26 semaines
